Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgement and order passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Dahod dated 6/9/2005 passed in Criminal Appeal No.50 of 2004, by which the learned appellate court has dismissed the said appeal and has confirmed the judgement and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned trial court passed in Criminal Case No.620 of 1990 by which the petitioner was convicted for the offence under sections 2(1-A),(A)(M) and section 7(1)(4)(5) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act" for short) and the petitioner is sentenced to undergo six months' Simple Imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/- and in default, to undergo further Simple Imprisonment of 10 days, the petitioner has preferred the present Criminal Revision Application.

sentences.text: 2.00. That the petitioner herein was tried and convicted under section 16 of the Act for the offence under sections 2(1- A),(A)(M) and section 7(1)(4)(5) of the Act by the learned trial court vide judgement and order dated 3/1/2003 passed in Criminal Case No.620 of 1990 and was sentenced to undergo six months Simple Imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000/- and in default, to undergo further Simple Imprisonment of 10 days.

The said order was challenged by the accused - petitioner herein by filing Criminal Appeal before the learned Sessions Judge, Dahod, being Criminal Appeal No.50 of 2004, which came to be dismissed by the learned Sessions Judge, Dahod vide judgement and order dated 6/9/2005, thereby confirming the order of the learned trial court.
3.00. It is not in dispute that the charge against the HC-NIC Page 2 of 8 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:29:41 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/808/2005 JUDGMENT petitioner was only of sub-standardization of milk.

4.00. Mr.Y.V. Vaghela, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner - accused has submitted that though the petitioner has some case even on merits, he would be giving up the plea on merits and his only submission is about sentence imposed by the courts below.

He has, in this behalf, submitted that there has been an amendment in the Act by the Central Amendment Act No.
34 of 1976, whereby sections 51 & 52 have been added and under the said section, only fine is leviable.
Therefore, he has requested to maintain the conviction but impose reasonable fine in lieu of sentence imposed by the courts below.

In support of his above submission, Mr.Vaghela, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner accused has heavily relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court dated 17/3/2016 in the case of Nemi Chand Versus State of Rajasthan rendered in Criminal Appeal No.214 of 2016.

sentences.text: Having heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and considering the facts of the present case, it is not in dispute that the petitioner has been convicted under section 16 of the Act and the Charge against the petitioner accused was only of sub-standardization HC-NIC Page 3 of 8 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:29:41 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/808/2005 JUDGMENT of milk.
There was no allegation of any adulteration injurious to the health.
Therefore, the case would squarely fall under sections 51 & 52 of the Central Amendment Act No. 34 of 1976.

As observed hereinabove, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner accused is not challenging the impugned judgement and order of conviction on merits and is, as such, giving up plea on merits and his only submission is about the sentence imposed by the courts below.
6.01. Identical question came to be considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Nemi Chand (supra).

While considering the similar request made on behalf of the accused in the case where the accused was convicted for the offence under section 7(16) of the Act and charge against the accused was only about sub-standardization of the goods, the Hon'ble Supreme Court accepted the request of the accused to modify the sentence impose by the courts below by imposing fine.

While considering the aforesaid request, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as under :-
"2.
It is not in dispute that the charge against the appellant was only of sub-standardization of goods.

Mr. Sushil Kumar Jain, learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that though the appellant has some prima facie case even on merits, he would be giving up the plea on merits and his only submission is about the sentence which has been imposed by the courts below.

He has, in this behalf, argued that there has been an amendment in the Act by the Central Amendment Act 34 of 1976 whereby Section 16A was HC-NIC Page 4 of 8 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:29:41 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/808/2005 JUDGMENT added and under the said section, only a fine is leviable.

He has drawn our attention to the judgment of this Court in "T. Barai V. Henry Ah Hoe and Another"
[1983 (1) SCC 177] wherein this Court held that since the amendment was beneficial to the accused persons, it can be applied even with respect to earlier cases as well which are pending in the Court.

entities.text:
T. Barai V. Henry Ah Hoe and Another"
[1983 (1) SCC 177]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said judgment, the Court held as under :-
"22.
It is only retroactive criminal legislation that is prohibited under Article 20(1).

The prohibition contained in Article 20(1) is that no person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence prohibits nor shall he be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence.

It is quite clear that insofar as the Central Amendment Act creates new offences or enhances punishment for a particular type of offence no person can be convicted by such ex post facto law nor can the enhanced punishment prescribed by the amendment be applicable.
But insofar as the Central Amendment Act reduces the punishment for an offence punishable under Section 16(1)

3 (a) of the Act, there is no reason why the accused should not have the benefit of such reduced punishment.

sentences.text: The rule of beneficial construction requires that even ex post facto law of such a type should be applied HC-NIC Page 5 of 8 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:29:41 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/808/2005 JUDGMENT to mitigate the rigour of the law.
The principle is based both on sound reason and common sense.
This finds support in the following passage from Craies on Statute Law, 7th Edn., at pp. 388-89:
A retrospective statute is different from an ex post facto statute.
"Every ex post facto law...." said Chase, J., in the American case of Calder v. Bull "must necessarily be retrospective, but every retrospective law is not an ex post facto law.

Every law that takes away or impairs rights vested agreeably to existing laws is retrospective, and is generally unjust and may be oppressive; it is a good general rule that a law should have no retrospect, but in cases in which the laws may justly and for the benefit of the community and also of individuals relate to a time antecedent to their commencement: as statutes of oblivion or of pardon.

They are certainly retrospective,
and literally both concerning and after the facts committed.

But I do not consider any law ex post facto within the prohibition that mollifies the rigour of the criminal law,
but only those that create or aggravate the crime, or increase the punishment or change the rules of evidence for the purpose of conviction....
There is a great and apparent difference between making an unlawful act lawful and the making an innocent action criminal and punishing it as a crime."
HC-NIC Page 6 of 8 Created On Mon Oct 02 03:29:41 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/808/2005 JUDGMENT
From the facts of the present case, we have no doubt in mind that the aforesaid judgment squarely applies thereon.
This appeal is, therefore, partly allowed and the sentence imposed upon the appellant is modified by imposing fine of Rs. 50,000/- which shall be deposited within two months with the trial court.
On deposit of the aforesaid amount, the bail bonds furnished by the appellant shall be discharged."
6.02. In view of the above, present Criminal Revision Application is partly allowed.

The sentence imposed upon the petitioner by the learned trial court confirmed by the learned sessions Judge is hereby modified by imposing fine of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) which shall be deposited by the petitioner accused within a period of four weeks from today with the learned trial court.
On deposit of the aforesaid amount, Bail Bonds furnished by the petitioner accused shall be discharged.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct Service is permitted.
